about: A simple library for making games in C, popular with beginners and teachers.

prs.title: File type checks no longer read dots in folder names
prs.broken: When asked for a file's type, raylib looked for the last dot anywhere in the path. A file with no type inside a folder like "assets.v2" came back as type ".v2/readme", so a game could pick the wrong loader.
prs.changed: It now looks only at the file's own name. Sound loading also handles a file with no type instead of crashing.
prs.matters: Games load their files correctly no matter how the folders are named.

prs.title: Blending between two rotations no longer takes the long way round
prs.broken: raylib's quick rotation blend missed that two rotations can point the same way with opposite signs. It then turned the long way round, and blending a rotation with its mirror copy gave an empty result.
prs.changed: It now flips the second rotation first in that case, the same check the smooth blend already did, so the two agree.
prs.matters: Animations and cameras that blend rotations no longer spin the wrong way or break.

prs.title: Turning a rotation into angles keeps all three at a straight-up pitch
prs.broken: When a rotation pointed straight up or down, raylib's conversion to angles lost the turn around the other axis and reported 0, so turning the angles back gave a different rotation.
prs.changed: At that point the whole turn now goes into one angle, so nothing is lost. Away from it the results are exactly the same as before.
prs.matters: Cameras and objects that look straight up or down keep their heading when code goes through angles.
